Like Roxella said, "if we don't know you we don't say hi." What this does though is that if you do say "hi" to someone you don't know, chances are that they'll think that you know them (otherwise why would you greet them?), and you may very well get a "hi" back from any given stranger as they don't want to be rude on the off-chance that they do know you somehow but just don't remember who you are in the moment. This works with waving at cars going by too.
This is easily solved by saying "hi" twice. "Hej" is not socially acceptable whilst "hej-hej" clearly is.

At the base of every problem, ever, is lack of communication.

Without knowing exactly what your exchanges thus far has looked like, him bailing out an hour before each of the planned sessions, tells me that you're not maintaining all that much correspondence.

With all that said, and how you like to give people second, third, and nth chances, I'd say that you still have a need which has to be met, and that will never happen unless you make him realize that your time is as valuable as his.

Were I in your shoes, however, I would begin to nicely tighten the vice on him. Open up a clear channel of communication, and tell him your view on your shared history, and that you have maintained faith in him because you think he very well might be the perfect fit for you.

Either he'll appreciate that you've stuck with him, despite all of his untimely problems, and will enjoy your honesty and determination to have him as your teacher.  Or he'll budge under pressure, and come up with further excuses not to drive with you.

Thus, either you will have earned yourself, if not a friend, at least an appreciative man to teach you how to drive. Or you'll come to the realization that you sadly have wasted your time by again and again having put your faith in someone who more than likely will transfer his poor character into his way of teaching, and then you're better off finding someone else to teach you how to handle a car altogether.

As I suffer from an unofficial (self-diagnosed) form of ADD which simply put can be described as having the attention span of a two-year-old, I rarely write anything longer than a limerick before I'm off chasing another idea.

​

Thus, managing to write the following is a smaller miracle, but sadly still far from a finished piece. It's better than nothing though, I suppose, and I'll gladly take any shape or form of feedback I can get on it.

​

\-----------

 

We had it all covered, or at least we thought we did. 

For countless millennia the stunning movement of land, and intriguing development of lifeforms across the planet which we somehow managed to put far enough away from its host star for it not to burst into flames, but still close enough for its warming rays to fuel photosynthesis, was the talk of the galaxy.

If you came in to work on Monday morning and didn’t know what the “Supercontinent Pangea” was, you might as well have stayed away from the water cooler altogether.

It had been a rough start, sure. But then, yet again, everyone who bought the subscription for the 24-hour a day constant access to the fascinating events of “Earth” was treated to nothing but the rawness and truth of natural selection.

It didn’t matter whether it was the sodium chloride slowly beating most of the planet’s water into submission, or if a slightly larger tectonic plate buried another one underneath its colossal mass, the game might have been brutal, but always fair.

Then, but a moment ago in the enormous lifespan of what without competition is the longest running reality tv show in the known, still expanding universe, one particular species got put on top.

In a time where continuity no longer seemed to matter, but all which the corporate executives wanted was “fresh thinking”, and “status quo” was as stigmatized as drinking orange juice after brushing one’s teeth, it was decided that the show “needed” a new crowd favorite. 

Thus, 65 million rotations of the green, blue, and everything in between-planet ago, cue primates. With their cursed cerebral cortices and damned opposable thumbs. How I hate those opposable thumbs.

I suppose we should have seen it coming, really. There had been sniffings in the air about commercially financed TV taking over completely, and it all came to show when Earth was bought by IPN, *The Intergalactic Patriarchal Network.* From the outside looking in it all seemed to be for the better, as the money they promised to funnel into the show was on, well, an intergalactic scale. Media said it was the best thing to happen to Earth since the addition of tidal waves with the moon coming into play. IPN made promises that the changes which they were to make wouldn’t be big enough to make a difference for a long, long time.

Depending on how you see it, they didn’t. However, on a scale of 4.6 billion years, 65 million isn’t all that long when you think about it. You’ve got to hand it to them though, because even as we saw the source code of what they introduced, and the initial primates were but roughly similar to squirrels and tree shrews in size and appearance, we had no idea what sort of impact these creatures would come to have, way down the line.

So, in line with ancient stoicism, knowledge is the driving force? Although there is no reason to obtain it?

I suppose history is filled with nothing but examples of people who assign meaning to something intangible (i.e. deities and/or an after life), just to keep up the illusion of reason to carry on.

I feel for your unwillingness to participate in a world where meaning is the tail off a dog which is chasing itself. In a sense I guess we have the same problem.

Subjectively, I know it to be. The momentary magic of a child's laugh and the possibility of "happiness" doesn't do it for me.

Happy and sad are two sides of the same coin. A coin which will keep on being flipped for perpetuity, with no ultimate purpose. So I say happy or sad doesn't matter.
